status_summary: Executive Order 14182 of 2025-01-24 revoked Executive Orders 14076 and 14079, the latter being the August 2022 order that pressed HHS to consider Section 1115 waivers for abortion travel. On 2025-01-27 the acting HHS Secretary announced that the Office for Civil Rights would review whether HHS programs, regulations and guidance comply with the Hyde Amendment. On 2025-07-11 the Office of Legal Counsel withdrew its 2022 opinion and concluded that the Hyde Amendment bars HHS funding of ancillary services such as transportation to obtain an abortion, outside the enumerated exceptions.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14182, Enforcing the Hyde Amendment, signed; it revokes Executive Orders 14076 and 14079 (published 2025-01-31).
HHS announces an OCR review of whether its programs, regulations and guidance comply with the Hyde Amendment.
DOJ Office of Legal Counsel issues an opinion withdrawing its 2022 Hyde Amendment opinion and concluding Hyde bars funding of transportation to obtain abortions.

OMB, with participating agencies, publishes a proposed rule, Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance (91 FR 32198; comments due 2026-07-13), rewriting the federal grant rules in 2 CFR part 200; its table of contents lists a new cost-principle section 200.477 titled Abortion. The section text was not read.

title: Withdraw Biden-era abortion travel funding actions and the OLC Hyde opinion
uncertainties: No published results of an HHS Hyde compliance audit were found, and no CMS Medicaid guidance or Section 1115 approval for abortion travel was found either to have been issued or withdrawn. The HHS review announcement is known from a news report rather than an HHS release. OCR rescissions in January 2026 cite the executive order but are tracked in another record. The text of proposed 2 CFR 200.477 could not be read: the Federal Register full-text, plain-text and GovInfo copies all end, as fetched, in the subpart C discussion. Only the section's title (Abortion) and the comment deadline are confirmed on the Federal Register page. A law-firm article says the section would make the costs of elective abortions unallowable under federal awards, and a link to Executive Order 14182 appears only in an advocacy group's comment letter; neither was confirmed in primary text. The proposal is not final.
